sprint_note: Makes FSRS the sole scheduler (removes Classic + the Sprint10 A/B experiment entirely, including its schema columns, dashboard, and badge; one-time Python-side FSRS-state initialization for cards with real pre-FSRS review history, named as an explicit approximation); replaces the removed writing-maturity concept with a derived 0-4 essay learning-progress level (four independently-gated milestones, two of them driven by a new guided/unguided exam_type split on oral examinations); consolidates essay/section button rows into a primary+dropdown pattern and adds a persisted category collapse/expand control on the overview page; and reworks the stats page (activity, workload/upcoming, observed recall with sample size, scheduled-interval distribution, essay learning progress) plus the flat main nav into a primary/secondary grouping using the Shell's existing mobile secondaryMenu mechanism.
summary: Collapses EssayCards onto a single FSRS scheduler, replaces the ad-hoc essay-maturity signal with a derived 0-4 learning-progress level built from card-coverage and guided/unguided oral-exam milestones, consolidates the app's button surface into a primary+action-menu pattern with a persisted category collapse control, and reworks the stats page and main navigation around the app's existing Dataset/chart and Shell nav contracts.

classification.why_application: Which single scheduling algorithm drives this app's own next_due_at, how 'essay learning progress' is defined from this app's own card/exam vocabulary, and how this app's own screens are organized are EssayCards-specific domain and UX decisions with no meaning outside this app's existing due-queue/essay/exam model (CLAUDE.md).
non_goals: FSRS parameter optimization or per-card/per-essay scheduler configuration (unchanged from Sprint10's non-goals)
Habit tracker (explicitly out of scope per 00_draft.md)
Recreating or modifying the already-deleted Descartes essay/flashcards
Changing due-queue selection, filtering, grouping, or ordering rules themselves (only the mechanism that produces next_due_at changes — see contracts.invariants)

True FSRS state reconstruction for cards with real pre-FSRS review history (no complete per-review rating history exists to replay; a named, documented approximation is used instead — see contracts.invariants)
A UI control for the FSRS desired-retention setting (it becomes a server-side configurable constant, not an end-user-facing control, this sprint)

An exposed FSRS-predicted-retrievability metric on the stats page (the draft's 'distinguish observed recall from FSRS predictions' is satisfied by clearly labeling the existing schedule-forecast block as a forecast, not by inventing a new predicted-retention number)

A true visual nav-grouping UI in Atlas_Shell's desktop sidebar (the Shell's AppConfig/NavItem contract has no group concept today — see contracts.failure_modes and open_questions; this sprint groups via the Shell's existing mobile secondaryMenu plus desktop ordering only, and surfaces the gap rather than extending the Shell)
Changing essays.status ('planned'/'complete') — preserved exactly as-is; it is pre-existing infrastructure, not the 'writing maturity' being replaced (see contracts.invariants)
classification.not_platform: The FSRS-only scheduling decision, the learning-level derivation, the guided/unguided exam split, and the button/nav consolidation are all meaningful only in terms of EssayCards' own due-queue, essay, section, and exam vocabulary (CLAUDE.md). None of this is a reusable technical capability — it does not generalize beyond this app's own domain model. Where this sprint touches genuinely reusable rendering (charts, the Shell's nav mechanism), it consumes existing 02_Platform capabilities (platform-ui BarChart/LineChart, Atlas_Shell's AppConfig) rather than building new platform surface.

VERIFICATION READING (Phase A investigation A2, binding): 'Selection and ordering behave identically for identical card data' means identical card data run through the SAME (now FSRS-only) scheduler — NOT that FSRS's own next_due_at/review_interval output must numerically match historical Classic output for a given card. Switching a formerly-Classic card to FSRS WILL change its future review_interval values and therefore its new/learning/established classification and BACKLOG sort position, purely as a side effect of different interval math, with zero selection/ordering code touched. This is expected and allowed by 00_draft.md ('different due dates will naturally affect which cards qualify; do not change the selection rules themselves') and must not be read as a regression by the test-runner.

essays.status ('planned'/'complete') is preserved exactly as-is, unchanged by this sprint — it is pre-existing infrastructure (Sprint07), not the 'writing maturity' concept being replaced. No code path in this sprint reads, writes, or derives from status differently than before.

FSRS desired_retention is a server-side setting, not a per-request value: ESSAYCARDS_FSRS_DESIRED_RETENTION (float, default 0.9), read ONCE at backend/scheduling.py import time into a module constant DESIRED_RETENTION, used to construct both the module-level fsrs.Scheduler(desired_retention=DESIRED_RETENTION) singleton and (as the SAME value) the one-time legacy FSRS-state migration's stability-inversion math — no UI exposure this sprint (see classification.non_goals).

LEGACY FSRS-STATE MIGRATION APPROXIMATION (named risk, R-OPS-BP-01 — must not be presented as exact): for every flashcard_review_state row with last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL and no existing fsrs_card_state row (i.e. every card that was reviewed under a non-FSRS-native path before this sprint, regardless of its prior Sprint10 scheduler assignment), a one-time Python migration (backend/migrate_fsrs_state.py, run at every startup after schema.sql, guarded by the same 'no existing fsrs_card_state row' condition so a rerun after the first successful pass touches zero rows) synthesizes initial FSRS state because no complete per-review rating history exists anywhere in the schema to replay (review_events is Sprint10-only and append-only; nothing predates it). The synthesis, computed by backend/scheduling.py::estimate_initial_fsrs_state(review_interval, last_reviewed_at, desired_retention) — a pure, independently unit-testable function: (a) stability — inverts FSRS-6's published interval-from-stability-and-retention relation (interval_days = (stability_days / FACTOR) * (desired_retention^(1/DECAY) - 1), FACTOR=19/81, DECAY=-0.5, the fixed forgetting-curve constants used by FSRS v4.5 onward, distinct from the trainable per-model weight vector) using the card's CURRENT review_interval; the implementer must confirm these constants (names/values) against the installed fsrs==6.3.2 source before coding, since silent drift would produce a wrong initial stability — floor stability_days at a small positive minimum (the library's own minimum, if exposed, else 0.01) to avoid non-positive values for very short intervals; (b) difficulty — no backward-derivable signal exists (depends on per-review grade history this app has never persisted), so it is obtained by running the module-level FSRS Scheduler's own review_card ONCE on a fresh fsrs.Card() with a neutral Rating.Good — i.e. exactly what a brand-new card's difficulty becomes after one average review — rather than hand-deriving a numeric constant, so it stays correct automatically if the installed library version ever changes; (c) fsrs_state — 2 (Review) if review_interval >= 24h else 1 (Learning), matching this app's existing established/learning threshold; (d) step — null for Review-state, 0 for Learning-state; (e) last_review_at — the card's existing last_reviewed_at, used as-is, never recomputed; (f) raw_state — MUST be produced by constructing an fsrs.Card with these fields and calling its own .to_dict() (never a hand-assembled dict literal), so it stays structurally valid for Card.from_dict() on every subsequent real review regardless of library internals. Every field of this synthesized state is a documented approximation, not a reconstruction of real review history — stated explicitly in code comments and in this document, never silently presented as exact (R-OPS-BP-01).

BACKUP BEFORE MIGRATION: before schema.sql drops any Sprint10 scheduler-assignment column, it creates essaycards.pre_fsrs_migration_backup_sprint12 (guarded by an information_schema table-existence check, so it is created exactly once and a rerun after the first successful run is a no-op) snapshotting flashcard_id, scheduler, scheduler_assigned_at, scheduler_assignment_reason, experiment_version, last_reviewed_at, next_due_at, review_interval, and a backed_up_at timestamp for every flashcard_review_state row as it stood immediately before migration. This table is new durable state (R-CON-BP-03): owned by this sprint, retained indefinitely as an audit trail, not automatically pruned (retention policy explicitly deferred — see deferred_decisions).

MIGRATION SAFE TO RERUN: every migration step in this sprint (schema.sql's column drops/additions, the backup-table creation, and the Python FSRS-state backfill) is naturally idempotent via its own existence/absence guard — a second run after a successful first run touches zero rows and makes zero additional changes. No step depends on run order across restarts beyond the single-transaction ordering within one schema.sql execution (backup before column drop) and schema.sql completing before the Python backfill runs (the backfill needs the final post-migration schema, in particular fsrs_card_state already existing).

DUE DATES PRESERVED: no migration step in this sprint (schema or Python) ever writes next_due_at, review_interval, or last_reviewed_at for an existing card — those three columns are read-only inputs to the FSRS-state synthesis, never targets of it (mirrors Sprint10's identical invariant).

VERIFY BEFORE REMOVING DEAD CODE: the implementer must confirm (via the test suite — see 10_test_spec.md) that the migration preserves due dates/review history and that FSRS review dispatch + rating mapping behave correctly BEFORE deleting backend/scheduling.py's ClassicScheduler/compute_next_due_at/decide_scheduler_assignment and backend/routers/experiment.py (00_draft.md §1 'Verify migration and rating mapping before removing the old scheduler's active code paths').

LEARNING-LEVEL MILESTONE DEFINITIONS (R-CON-AL-01/03 closure-complete; all four computed fresh at query time against Postgres now(), never cached/stored — R-CON-AL-06): 'active card' = every flashcard currently belonging to the essay (EssayCards has no archival/retirement concept for cards — every card is 'active' by construction; this is a definition decision, not a new column). Milestone 1 (cards seen): progress_total > 0 AND every card has last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL (cards_seen_count == progress_total). Milestone 2 (cards future-safe): progress_total > 0 AND every card has last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL AND next_due_at > now() + interval '24 hours' (cards_future_safe_count == progress_total) — the comparison basis is Postgres now() at query time, the same server-clock authority every other derived essay field already uses. Milestone 3 (guided passed): the essay has at least one section, every section has at least one exam_type='guided' examination, AND every section's LATEST guided examination has score >= 3 (a per-section minimum gate, not an average — 'passed' is a true/false fact about every section, not a blended score). Milestone 4 (unguided passed): identical to milestone 3 with exam_type='unguided'. Both milestones 1 and 2 are explicitly false (never vacuously true) for an essay with zero cards, satisfying 00_draft.md's 'essays without active cards must not automatically satisfy the card milestones'. learning_level = the count of these four booleans that are true (0-4); no fixed completion order is required or enforced.

'Passed' threshold: a section_examinations.score of 3 or higher counts as passed for milestones 3/4 — matches the existing EXAM_PROMPT_INTRO's own scoring rubric language ('3: functional understanding — good enough for now, ready to move on'). This numeric threshold is a named design decision (PASS_SCORE_THRESHOLD = 3), not left implicit.

guided_passed_at / unguided_passed_at mirror the pre-existing oral_date's 'oldest wins' semantics applied per exam_type: the OLDEST examined_at among each section's latest-examination-of-that-type rows, present only when that milestone is true. Re-examining one stale section of a given type moves that type's passed_at forward to whichever section of that type is stalest next — same mechanic as the removed oral_date, just split by exam_type.

GUIDED vs UNGUIDED EXAM_TYPE is a closed, required, never-defaulted field on every section_examinations row going forward (section_examinations.exam_type, CHECK in ('guided','unguided'), existing pre-sprint rows backfilled to 'guided' by column DEFAULT — a reasonable historical assumption since every pre-sprint exam used the one existing calibration-aware flow, which is what 'guided' means). POST /examinations/import requires exam_type explicitly on every result, with NO silent default — same precedent as POST /flashcards/upsert's required, never-defaulted card.level (R-CON-AL-04 discipline: a silently-defaulted exam_type could misclassify an unguided exam as guided or vice versa, silently corrupting milestone 3/4).

GET /essays/{essay_id}/examination-package's exam_type query parameter is REQUIRED but implemented as an optional (defaulted-None) FastAPI parameter manually validated to api_error VALIDATION_ERROR when missing or not in ('guided','unguided') — never a bare required FastAPI query param, which would produce FastAPI's own 422 shape instead of ApiError (same discipline already applied to every raw-Request-body endpoint in this app).

exam_type='unguided' means the examination-package's per-section last_examination field is ALWAYS null, regardless of actual prior history — 'unguided' is defined as 'no calibration context passed to the LLM', not merely 'no unguided history exists yet'. exam_type='guided' computes last_examination from the latest exam_type='guided' row per section only (never mixing in unguided rows) — the independent-gating requirement from Phase A investigation A3.

All read endpoints returning UI-visible tabular data continue to return Dataset per R-CON-BP-04 (list/detail essays, section examinations, review-stats summary/activity/intervals). GET /examination-package remains the pre-existing R-CON-BP-04 bespoke-JSON exemption (clipboard/LLM interchange artifact, unchanged rationale).

Button consolidation preserves every action listed in the top-level §button_nav_inventory block below — none is dropped, only regrouped into a primary action + secondary dropdown at the section end and the essay header (see §button_nav_inventory for the exact per-action mapping). Category collapse/expand state is persisted via localStorage, keyed per category name (UNCATEGORIZED for the null-category group), defaulting to expanded when no stored value exists — the heading row (title, established/total, open count, the existing per-category Study button) remains visible when collapsed; only the essay rows beneath it hide.

Nav grouping respects the Shell's actual AppConfig contract (R-CON-BP-06): mobilePrimaryNav keeps only the everyday-learning + stats items (Essays, Due for review, Stats — 3 of the max 5), content-management (Add / Update Essay) moves to secondaryMenu (the Shell's existing mobile 'More' overlay). The desktop Sidebar renders desktopNav as a flat ordered list with no grouping concept in the current Shell contract — this sprint achieves 'grouping' on desktop only via adjacent `order` values, and does not add a group field to NavItem/AppConfig (that would violate R-CON-BP-06 and the Shell's own stable integration-contract versioning note). True visual sidebar grouping would require a Platform-layer Atlas_Shell change — explicitly out of scope, surfaced as an open question instead of silently invented.

FSRS-state backfill per-row failure (backend/migrate_fsrs_state.py) — each row is backfilled in its own small transaction so one malformed/unexpected historical row logs an error and is skipped rather than blocking every other card's migration or startup entirely; a skipped row remains without fsrs_card_state until its next real review, at which point FSRSScheduler.review starts it from a fresh fsrs.Card() exactly as it would for a never-reviewed card (same safe fallback, not a hard failure)

internal_flow.name: fsrs_only_review_dispatch
internal_flow.description: review_flashcard (backend/routers/flashcards.py) no longer reads or branches on a `scheduler` column (removed). It always loads existing fsrs_card_state (nullable — None for a card's first-ever review), always calls FSRSScheduler().review(grade, last_reviewed_at, now, existing_state), always writes flashcard_review_state (unchanged three columns), always upserts fsrs_card_state, and always inserts one review_events row (scheduler column removed from review_events) — all inside the same existing transaction.
outputs: SchedulerResult
flashcard_review_state updated
fsrs_card_state upserted
review_events row inserted

internal_flow.name: new_card_seeding_simplified
internal_flow.description: The three was_inserted-gated flashcard_review_state INSERTs (backend/ingest.py::_upsert_flashcard, backend/routers/flashcards.py::_upsert_question, backend/exploration.py::execute_plan's create_card loop) drop all scheduler-assignment logic/columns — a bare INSERT of (flashcard_id, last_reviewed_at=null, next_due_at=created_at, review_interval='0' where applicable). No decide_scheduler_assignment call anywhere.
outputs: flashcard_review_state row seeded, no scheduler metadata

internal_flow.name: schema_migration_backup_and_drop
internal_flow.description: schema.sql, in order within its existing single transaction: (a) create essaycards.pre_fsrs_migration_backup_sprint12 if it does not yet exist, snapshotting every flashcard_review_state row's scheduler-related + scheduling columns; (b) drop flashcard_review_state.scheduler/scheduler_assigned_at/scheduler_assignment_reason/experiment_version (their CHECK constraints and single/multi-column indexes referencing only these columns are dropped automatically by Postgres along with the columns); (c) drop review_events.scheduler (same automatic constraint/index cleanup); (d) add section_examinations.exam_type (not null, default 'guided', CHECK in ('guided','unguided')) — additive, idempotent `add column if not exists`.
outputs: backup table populated (once)
scheduler columns gone
exam_type column present, pre-sprint rows defaulted to 'guided'

internal_flow.name: legacy_fsrs_state_backfill
internal_flow.description: backend/migrate_fsrs_state.py, invoked once at every startup immediately after init_schema() completes: selects every flashcard_review_state row with last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL and no existing fsrs_card_state row, computes initial state via backend.scheduling.estimate_initial_fsrs_state(review_interval, last_reviewed_at, DESIRED_RETENTION) per card, and INSERTs the resulting fsrs_card_state row in its own per-row transaction (so one bad row logs and is skipped, not a startup-blocking failure). Naturally idempotent — a rerun selects zero rows once every eligible card has a state row.
outputs: fsrs_card_state rows for every pre-FSRS-native reviewed card

internal_flow.name: experiment_removal
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/experiment.py deleted; its import/include_router call removed from main.py. backend/scheduling.py loses ClassicScheduler, compute_next_due_at, decide_scheduler_assignment, EXPERIMENT_VERSION, _SCHEDULER_ASSIGNMENT_REASONS, _AGAIN_INTERVAL, _FLOORS. VALID_GRADES and SchedulerResult survive (still meaningful with one scheduler).
outputs: dead experimental code removed, after step 1-4 are verified per contracts.invariants

internal_flow.name: learning_progress_query
internal_flow.description: A shared SQL shape (used by both list_essays' per-row LATERAL join and get_essay's single-essay equivalent) computes, per essay: cards_seen_count, cards_future_safe_count (both against now()), and, via two per-exam_type LATERAL subqueries over section_examinations (latest row per section, filtered by exam_type), guided_passed/guided_passed_at and unguided_passed/unguided_passed_at (per-section minimum score >= 3, all sections required, oldest-examined-at-wins for the date) — see contracts.invariants for the exact closure rules. The four booleans (milestone_all_cards_seen, milestone_all_cards_future_safe, milestone_guided_passed, milestone_unguided_passed) are then summed into learning_level (0-4).
outputs: nine derived fields per essay

internal_flow.name: exam_type_threaded_export
internal_flow.description: backend/examinations.py::build_export_package gains a required exam_type parameter. For exam_type='guided', the last_exam_by_section lookup filters section_examinations on exam_type='guided' (same shape as before, now type-scoped). For exam_type='unguided', last_exam_by_section is always empty (no calibration context) — this is a deliberate skip, not a query returning no rows by coincidence. The package gains a top-level exam_type field.
outputs: export package, scoped to exam_type

internal_flow.name: exam_type_threaded_import
internal_flow.description: backend/examinations.py::validate_import_body requires exam_type on every result (no default, same discipline as POST /flashcards/upsert's required card.level); import_results' INSERT includes exam_type in the column list.
outputs: section_examinations rows carrying exam_type

internal_flow.name: essay_header_action_menu
internal_flow.description: ReaderView's top button row becomes: a standalone '← All essays' back button (unchanged, never bundled into the menu) plus a new ActionMenu whose primary action is Study (focus session on the whole essay, when progress_total > 0) or, when the essay has no cards, falls back to Question overview as primary. Secondary dropdown items: Question overview (when not already primary), Guided oral exam, Unguided oral exam (both gated on status === 'complete', same gate the old per-essay Oral exam button used), Export essay / Import → (same toggle-to-Import pattern as before, now inside the menu), + New nugget (when sections.length > 0). The essay's learning_level (+ compact tooltip) renders near this header.
inputs: essay detail row (now carrying the nine learning-progress fields)
outputs: consolidated essay header, every pre-existing action preserved

internal_flow.name: section_end_action_menu
internal_flow.description: Each section's end-of-section button row becomes one ActionMenu: primary = Review this section (the everyday action); secondary dropdown = Export section / Import → and Insert section after / Import → (both keep their existing toggle-to-Import behavior, now surfaced via the existing sectionActionMsg panel below the menu rather than by mutating a button's own label, since a dropdown closes after selection). SectionExaminationHistory is unaffected — it sits below the menu exactly as before, now additionally showing each entry's exam_type.
outputs: consolidated per-section controls, every pre-existing action preserved

internal_flow.name: overview_per_essay_row_simplified
internal_flow.description: EssayListView's per-essay row drops its Study and Oral-exam buttons and the oral_score/oral_date line entirely; the row instead shows a compact learning_level badge (0-4) with a tooltip/accessible explanation of the four milestones. The row (title/click target) still navigates into ReaderView, where Study and both oral-exam variants now live (step 9). handleExportExam/examMsg/examBusyId state moves from EssayListView to ReaderView along with the oral-exam action.
inputs: essay overview rows (now carrying learning_level + milestone fields)
outputs: simplified per-essay row

internal_flow.name: category_collapse_toggle
internal_flow.description: Each category heading in EssayListView gains a collapse/expand toggle button (visible chevron + accessible label, same ▸/▾ visual convention SectionExaminationHistory already uses), reading/writing localStorage key essaycards:categoryCollapsed:<category> ('true'/'false'; UNCATEGORIZED for the null-category group). Default expanded when no stored value exists. The heading row (title, established/total, open count, existing per-category Study button) always stays visible; only the essay rows beneath collapse/hide.
outputs: per-category collapsed state, persisted across visits

internal_flow.name: stats_page_rework
internal_flow.description: FORECAST_COLUMNS' rendering is first extracted out of ReviewStatsPanel into a new, props-decoupled sub-component, ForecastGrid (props: rows: {label: string; values: (number | null)[]}[] — no topic/essayId/sectionId/refreshToken/reviewed/backlog/newRemaining/sessionForecast). ReviewStatsPanel keeps its own 'Current' zone and its GET /flashcards/stats(scope) fetch exactly as before, but now renders its 'Upcoming' grid by calling ForecastGrid with rows=[{label:'All', values: allRow}, {label:'Session', values: sessionRow}] — visually and behaviorally identical to the pre-extraction markup. ReviewStatsView then fetches, in parallel: GET /review-stats/summary (existing, unchanged), GET /review-stats/activity (new), GET /review-stats/intervals (new), GET /essays (existing, reused — essay learning-progress histogram is computed client-side by bucketing rows on learning_level, 0-4, no new backend endpoint), and GET /flashcards/stats with no scope params (system-wide forecast, same endpoint ReviewStatsPanel already calls, just without topic/essay_id/section_id). Renders four clearly labeled zones: 'Study activity' (platform-ui LineChart over the activity Dataset), 'Scheduled reviews (forecast)' (ForecastGrid with rows=[{label:'All', values: allRow}] only — no Session row, since the stats page has no active review session — explicitly labeled as a schedule forecast, not an observed fact), 'Observed recall' (the existing ReviewStatsCard day/week/month cards, explicitly labeled 'observed' with sample size = reviews count and period named per card), 'Scheduled intervals' (platform-ui BarChart over the intervals Dataset), and 'Essay learning progress' (a small five-bar histogram, levels 0-4, built client-side from GET /essays). ExperimentDashboardView, its route, and its nav entry are removed.
inputs: five GET responses (summary, activity, intervals, essays, system-wide flashcards/stats)
outputs: ForecastGrid extracted and shared by ReviewStatsPanel + ReviewStatsView
reworked stats page, obsolete experiment statistics removed

internal_flow.name: nav_regrouping

risks.risk: The legacy FSRS-state migration's stability/difficulty synthesis is a documented approximation, not a reconstruction of real review history — a card's true memory state (what the user actually remembers) may differ from what the formula infers from its current review_interval alone.
risks.impact: Expected and accepted per 00_draft.md ('handle missing or incompatible historical data explicitly') — FSRS self-corrects from real reviews going forward; flagged in the sprint summary as a known limitation, not a defect.

risks.risk: Switching every card to FSRS changes future review_interval values, and therefore BACKLOG ordering and established/learning classification, for every formerly-Classic card.
risks.impact: Expected per 00_draft.md itself; see contracts.invariants' VERIFICATION READING entry — must not be mistaken for a selection-logic regression during test review.

risks.risk: The guided/unguided per-section-minimum 'passed' gate is strict — a single weak section blocks the whole essay's milestone 3/4, even if every other section scores highly.
risks.impact: A deliberate design choice (see deferred_decisions) favoring a clear pass/fail semantic over an averaged score; could feel punitive for large essays with many sections — a candidate for product feedback after this sprint ships.

risks.risk: Desktop sidebar nav 'grouping' is order-only (no visual separation) because the Shell contract has no group concept.
risks.impact: The draft's 'group related functions together' is only partially realized on desktop; fully realized on mobile via secondaryMenu. Surfaced explicitly rather than silently worked around (R-OPS-BP-01) — see open_questions.

risks.risk: A single malformed historical flashcard_review_state row (last_reviewed_at not null, no fsrs_card_state) could repeatedly fail the per-row FSRS-state backfill on every startup if the failure is not transient.
risks.impact: That one card falls back to fresh-Card() initialization on its next real review (same safe path as a never-reviewed card) rather than ever getting its interval-derived approximation — a narrower, self-healing degradation, not a startup failure.

open_questions.question: Should Atlas_Shell's AppConfig/NavItem contract gain a real grouping concept for the desktop sidebar, so future sprints (in any app) don't have to simulate grouping via ordering alone?
Should the per-section 'passed' gate for guided/unguided milestones become configurable (minimum vs. average) in a future sprint?
Should GET /review-stats/activity eventually respect the reviewer's local timezone instead of fixed UTC calendar days?
